title: Ross Stores (ROST) Dips More Than Broader Market: What You Should Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: Ross Stores stock declined 1.13% on September 29, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500's 0.17% loss. Despite the daily dip, ROST has gained 3.74% over the past month, outperforming its sector. The company is expected to report Q3 EPS of $1.82 (up 15.19% YoY) and annual earnings of $8.77 per share (up 32.68% YoY). ROST holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating with a Forward P/E of 27.03, trading at a premium to its industry average.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite a minor daily decline, ROST demonstrates strong fundamentals with expected EPS growth of 15.19% quarterly and 32.68% annually. The stock has outperformed its sector over the past month (+3.74% vs -6.36% sector loss), carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating, and analyst estimates have been revised upward by 0.92% over the past month, indicating improving business outlook.

title: Macy's Digital Push Gains Traction as AI & Omnichannel Efforts Expand
author: Zacks.Com
description: Macy's is strengthening its digital capabilities and AI integration across its omnichannel strategy. Digital penetration reached 31% of net sales in Q2 FY2026, with the Ask Macy's AI assistant expanding to in-store colleagues. The company raised its fiscal 2026 outlook, expecting net sales of $21.68-$21.83 billion and comparable sales growth of 1-1.5%, supported by improved operational metrics including a 7% increase in units processed per hour.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Macy's demonstrated strong execution with digital penetration at 31% of sales, raised fiscal 2026 guidance, improved operational metrics (7% increase in units processed per hour, 6.7% improvement in order-to-ship days), and successful AI integration through Ask Macy's expansion. Stock has outperformed industry benchmarks with 30.9% six-month gains.

title: Burlington's Beauty & Accessories Categories Lead Sales Trends
author: Na
description: Burlington Stores reported Q2 sales growth of 11% to nearly $3B with 2% comparable-store sales increase, driven by higher average basket sizes despite flat transaction counts. The company plans 115 net new stores and will reinvest $55M in tariff refunds to boost values. Management expects 3-4% comparable-store sales growth in fiscal 2026, with beauty and accessories performing strongly. However, the key challenge remains converting merchandise momentum into increased customer traffic.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Q2 results showed solid 11% sales growth and positive merchandise margin expansion, the company carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating. The critical concern is flat transaction counts despite rising basket sizes, indicating customer traffic remains weak. Management's reliance on tariff refunds to drive future growth and the need to convert category momentum into repeat visits suggest cautious optimism rather than strong conviction.

Target carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with consensus estimates suggesting 37.8% earnings growth and 5% sales growth. The company delivered a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 10.5%, demonstrating consistent outperformance of expectations.

Dollar Tree holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with consensus estimates indicating 34.6% earnings growth and 6.7% sales growth. The company delivered a trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise of 12.2%, showing strong execution.

Ross Stores maintains a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with consensus estimates projecting 32.7% earnings growth and 12.4% sales growth. The company delivered an 11.2% trailing four-quarter average earnings surprise, demonstrating consistent outperformance.

title: DG vs. ROST: Which Stock Is the Better Value Option?
author: Na
description: A comparison of Dollar General (DG) and Ross Stores (ROST) in the retail discount sector reveals that DG presents a better value opportunity. Both stocks hold a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with positive earnings outlooks, but DG's superior valuation metrics—including a forward P/E of 15.83 versus ROST's 25.83, and a P/B ratio of 2.91 versus ROST's 10.73—earn it a Value grade of A compared to ROST's D grade.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: DG demonstrates superior value metrics with a lower forward P/E ratio (15.83), lower PEG ratio (1.66), and significantly lower P/B ratio (2.91). It received a Value grade of A and is identified as the better value opportunity between the two stocks.

ROST holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) with positive earnings outlook, but its higher valuation multiples (forward P/E of 25.83, P/B of 10.73) and Value grade of D make it less attractive as a value investment compared to DG.

title: Best Buy's AI Push Drives Digital Growth & Retail Momentum
author: Na
description: Best Buy reported strong fiscal Q2 results with revenues up 3.6% year-over-year to $9.8 billion and comparable sales growth of 4.1%. The company is advancing its retail model through AI integration, experiential stores, and marketplace expansion. Computing sales led growth with a tenth consecutive quarter of positive comparable sales, while the Marketplace GMV forecast was raised to $1.3 billion. Best Buy stock has risen 26.5% over the past three months.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong Q2 revenue growth of 3.6% YoY, comparable sales up 4.1%, successful AI and marketplace initiatives, computing category showing tenth consecutive quarter of positive sales, stock up 26.5% in three months, and raised full-year Marketplace GMV forecast to $1.3 billion demonstrate solid operational momentum.
